stories.headline: Assam Flood Row: Akhil Gogoi Warns of March to PM's Residence as Stir Enters Day 8
stories.title: Assam Flood Row: Akhil Gogoi Warns of March to PM's Residence as Stir Enters Day 8
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The indefinite Satyagraha led by Raijor Dal president and Sivasagar MLA Akhil Gogoi crossed 158 hours and entered its eighth day on Friday, October 9, 2026.
Staged at the Assam Legislative Assembly premises, the protest demands ₹10 lakh compensation for every flood-affected family in Upper Assam and a CBI probe into the June flood crisis.
Gogoi spoke of expanding the agitation nationally with a massive march towards the Prime Minister’s residence in New Delhi.
The development follows high political drama on Day 7, when hundreds of Raijor Dal workers carrying black flags marched toward Janata Bhawan and the Assam CM's official residence.
Police intercepted the crowd, triggering minor scuffles and leading to the preventive detention of several protesters.

stories.headline: Vote Counting for Nagaon Lok Sabha Bye-Election Begins Today Amid Tight Preparations
stories.title: Vote Counting for Nagaon Lok Sabha Bye-Election Begins Today Amid Tight Preparations
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NAGAON: The Nagaon district administration has completed all preparations for the counting of votes for the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency bye-election, scheduled to be held on Friday.

Addressing a press conference on Thursday evening, District Commissioner and Returning Officer Aranyak Saikia said that counting of votes recorded through EVMs would be conducted simultaneously at three counting centres in Nagaon and Morigaon districts, while counting of postal ballots would be held separately at Dawson Higher Secondary Multipurpose School in Nagaon.
Counting will begin at 8 am with the opening of the strong rooms in the presence of representatives of all candidates and election observers.
Letters have already been sent to the candidates regarding the arrangements, the District Election Officer said.
There will be 14 counting tables in each Assembly constituency, operating simultaneously.
Depending on the constituency, counting will be conducted in 18 to 22 rounds.
Meanwhile, Assam Chief Electoral Officer Anurag Goel visited Nagaon again on Thursday to review preparations for the counting of votes.

stories.headline: BRS backs CEC's ouster: Can Opposition widen its campaign against the Election Commission?
stories.title: BRS backs CEC's ouster: Can Opposition widen its campaign against the Election Commission?
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bharat Rashtra Samithi has demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, adding to the Opposition's campaign over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

'Eternal vigilance is the price of liberty.' The famous words, often attributed to political thinker John Philpot Curran, underline the importance of protecting democratic institutions and citizens' rights, an argument now at the centre of the Opposition's campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) has joined the demand for Kumar's removal, adding another political voice to the Opposition's campaign ahead of its planned meeting with President Droupadi Murmu on Friday.
The development is significant because the party, led by K Chandrashekar Rao, is the principal Opposition force in Telangana, where the Congress is in power.

BRS working president and former Telangana minister K T Rama Rao announced the party's position on X, arguing that no individual should be above constitutional institutions or citizens' voting rights.
'Gyanesh Kumar must go!
No individual is above the institution,' Rao said, questioning why the political establishment should rally behind one individual when the rights of millions of Indians are at stake.

He also called for the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and order an independent investigation headed by a sitting judge.
The BRS's intervention broadens the political backing for the demand against Kumar beyond the parties spearheading the protests in Delhi.
The Congress has led the campaign, while the Trinamool Congress (TMC), headed by West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, has sought to build support among other Opposition parties.
People aware of the developments said the TMC had reached out to the BRS to garner support for Kumar's resignation.
The BRS's public statement signals agreement on this issue, even though the two parties have distinct political interests and operate in different states.

stories.headline: Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.title: Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.summary: Norway, Oct 9 : Indian-origin South African jurist and human rights pioneer Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for her efforts to promote peace and international law, the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced. In its official announcement on Friday, the committee said Pillay had demonstrated exceptional courage and integrity in advancing a more comprehensive global legal order and had played a significant role in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. “The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 goes to a person who with exceptional courage and integrity has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order. This year’s laureate has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted,” the press release stated. In a post on X announcing the award, the Nobel Prize account said, “Today Navi Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.” The Nobel Committee highlighted Pillay’s long career in advancing universal legal principles, from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who opposed apartheid in South Africa to her service as a judge in major international legal cases. “Born into a family of Indian Tamil origin under apartheid in Durban, South Africa, Pillay became a lawyer and legal pioneer, confronting deep structural discrimination, segregation and exclusion,” the committee said. Pillay has served as a judge on South Africa’s High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She also served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and, until recently, chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. She is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice in the case in which Myanmar stands accused of genocide, according to the Nobel Committee. The committee noted that Pillay had helped demonstrate how legal measures could prevent acts of war and violence while strengthening international legal institutions. In a post on X, the Nobel Prize account emphasised the importance of international law in addressing conflicts peacefully. “More and more conflicts are being addressed through diplomacy, treaties and legal mechanisms, rather than threats, violence and warfare. International law is a foundation for a more peaceful world,” the post said. It added, “At a time of existential challenges - including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time – international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity.” The Nobel Committee also highlighted Pillay’s contribution to landmark legal developments in the prosecution of sexual violence and genocide. “When the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda established that rape and sexual violence could constitute a crime against humanity – as well as genocide - her influence was a significant factor,” the committee said. It added that Pillay was instrumental in a separate legal breakthrough in the same case, in which a defendant faced charges of incitement to commit genocide purely based on "spreading propaganda". The committee said Pillay had held states and national leaders accountable while bringing hope to victims of violence and conflict. Throughout her career, she has emphasised the responsibility of individuals and states to comply with the rule of law. The award also comes amid what the committee described as growing pressure on the international legal system and its institutions. “We see a shift towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and global respect for law and justice. Whenever might overtakes right, it undermines stability, trust and peaceful co-existence,” the press release stated. Explaining the significance of the award, the committee said, “In awarding this year’s Nobel Peace Prize, the Norwegian Nobel Committee wants to remind the world that the rule of law - national and international - underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace and resolve conflicts non-violently. Peace requires justice.” The committee further said that Pillay’s career demonstrated the importance of protecting and expanding international legal principles. “Navi Pillay’s commitment to justice and human dignity is a source of hope and inspiration to all who seek to bring about a more peaceful world,” it said. The Nobel Committee said the 2026 Peace Prize was rooted in Alfred Nobel’s will, highlighting Pillay’s contribution to strengthening fraternity between nations and advancing the use of tribunals to promote peace and justice.

stories.headline: Green Stocks Oct 9- Dead Cat Bounce, Or Bottom? Monday May Bring a Verdict
stories.title: Green Stocks Oct 9- Dead Cat Bounce, Or Bottom? Monday May Bring a Verdict
stories.summary: As the markets made a sharp upmove today, a move that was not enough to make the week end on a positive note overall, the green pack made the most of the positivity as well. Interestingly, it was the two wind energy firms in our index, Inox Wind and Suzlon that rose sharply, perhaps a reflection of the immense beating their prices have taken in the past weeks.Adani Green or Tata Power, the two heavyweights, rose, but not enough to recover lost ground. Acme Solar, the outstanding story of the last quarter, also continued to drift lower. Solar manufacturers also got a respite of sorts, but the picture remains unclear. Monday will tell us if the markets have found bottom finally, or will the pain continue. With little to extoll on the oil prices front, the US piling on perceived weaknesses in the Indian economy to pressure the country for the trade deal, and of course, domestic fishing for trouble by way of questioning key institutions like the Election commission, a drop on Monday would be no surprise really. One only hopes the government is alive to the challenges, and takes the right decisions, which always translates to trusting your citizens to do the right thing when provided the opportunity to do so, trusting them to take the right call when provided information transparently, and of course avoiding inflammatory rhetoric. Is that too much to expect? We will know soon enough.

stories.headline: India’s logistics sector eyes $600 billion by 2031-32; cost pegged at 8% of GDP: DPIIT official
stories.title: India’s logistics sector eyes $600 billion by 2031-32; cost pegged at 8% of GDP: DPIIT official
stories.summary: Logistics contributed more than 13% to India’s GDP and played a critical role in supporting manufacturing growth
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India’s logistics sector is expected to double in size to $600 billion by 2031-32 from around $300 billion currently, driven by infrastructure development, policy reforms and improved connectivity, said Subhash Chandra Karol, Director, Logistics Division, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
Logistics contributed more than 13 per cent to India’s GDP and played a critical role in supporting manufacturing growth.

The two sectors were complementary, making efficient logistics infrastructure essential to strengthening the country’s manufacturing ecosystem, he said while addressing at PRISM 2026 – Powering Recognition: India’s Skill Movement, hosted by the Logistics Sector Skill Council (LSC) in association with National Skill Development Council on Friday.
A study conducted by DPIIT in 2025 estimated India’s logistics costs at around 8 per cent of GDP, challenging the earlier perception that they accounted for 13-14 per cent.
The reduction reflects the impact of government reforms and efforts to improve logistics efficiency, although the official noted that comparable estimates had not been available earlier.
India has also improved its position in the Logistics Performance Index (LPI), moving from 46th in 2018 to 30th.
The government aims to bring the country into the top 25 within the next five years, said Karol.
Infrastructure connectivity remains central to improving logistics efficiency, with better links needed between manufacturing hubs, consumption centres and last-mile destinations.
The government launched PM Gati Shakti in 2021 as a digital platform to coordinate infrastructure planning across ministries.

The platform helps identify gaps in connectivity, locate underserved areas and anticipate implementation hurdles, including forest areas and restricted zones, before projects reach the execution stage.
This enables authorities to plan clearances in advance and reduce delays during implementation, the official said.
The pace of road construction has increased from around 5-6 km a day to more than 15 km a day on average, according to the official.

stories.headline: Aravalli conservation: SC panel to survey forests and mines in Rajasthan
stories.title: Aravalli conservation: SC panel to survey forests and mines in Rajasthan
stories.summary: Jaipur, Oct 9 : The Supreme Court-appointed High-Powered Committee (HPC), tasked with examining the definition, ecological status and conservation of the Aravalli mountain range, will visit Rajasthan’s Vagad region from October 11 to 13. The committee will inspect the Paldeval-Sarkan area of Dungarpur district and the Kevadiya-Kothara area of Banswara district to assess ground realities concerning mining, forests, land use and the livelihoods of local communities, particularly tribal populations. The visit follows the committee’s tour of the Aravalli region in Gujarat from October 8 to 10. During its Rajasthan visit, the panel will conduct field inspections and interact with local residents and other stakeholders. Its findings will contribute to a comprehensive report that the Supreme Court has directed it to submit by November 30 this year. In an order dated May 25, 2026, the Supreme Court constituted a five-member High-Powered Committee chaired by the Director General of the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE). The committee was tasked with independently examining the previously-formulated definition of the Aravalli range and the process used to demarcate the hills based on that definition. The exercise is intended to assess the region’s ecological characteristics and address concerns relating to its conservation. The committee’s latest visit will focus on areas where the relationship between the Aravalli landscape, forest ecosystems, wildlife, mining activities and local livelihoods is particularly significant. The Rajasthan government has mobilised the Forest Department and local field officials ahead of the committee’s visit. A senior Forest Department official will serve as the field coordinator, while Deputy Conservators of Forests (DCFs) and other field personnel from Dungarpur and Banswara will accompany the panel during its inspections. The arrangements are intended to facilitate site visits, provide relevant field information and enable direct interaction between the committee and local stakeholders. The committee had earlier undertaken a five-day tour of Rajasthan, during which it conducted field inspections and consulted stakeholders at several locations. However, concerns were raised that participation had been inadequate, particularly among rural residents and tribal communities. This prompted calls for another ground-level assessment in southern Rajasthan, with greater emphasis on hearing directly from the people most affected by decisions concerning the Aravalli region. In its order dated September 7, the Supreme Court clarified that the committee must provide sufficient opportunities for all relevant stakeholders, including tribal communities in Rajasthan and Gujarat, to express their views. The panel is expected to incorporate these perspectives into its final assessment, which must be submitted to the Court by November 30. During the upcoming inspections, the committee will examine several aspects of the region’s environmental and economic landscape, including mining and quarrying activities, including stone-crushing operations, forest cover, water sources and surrounding ecological conditions, existing land-use patterns and their environmental implications, the impact of mining and land-use practices on local residents and tribal livelihoods. The committee will also seek feedback from environmentalists, subject experts, mining leaseholders, villagers, farmers, labourers and tribal communities. Evening consultations are planned in both districts, with approximately three hours allocated for discussions with local residents and other stakeholders on each day. According to the proposed schedule, the committee will complete its Gujarat tour by October 10 before entering southern Rajasthan on October 11. On October 11, there will be field inspections in the Paldeval-Sarkan area of Dungarpur district, followed by consultations with stakeholders. On October 12, inspection of the Kevadiya-Kothara area in Banswara district will be made followed by discussions with local communities and other stakeholders. October 13 will mark the final day of the scheduled Rajasthan visit. The inspections are expected to provide the committee with a clearer understanding of local environmental conditions, mining-related concerns and the socio-economic realities of communities living in the region. The findings will form part of the broader assessment of the Aravalli hills’ definition, demarcation and conservation. The committee’s report, due by November 30 this year, will be submitted to the Supreme Court for further consideration. --IANS

The committee had earlier undertaken a five-day tour of Rajasthan, during which it conducted field inspections and consulted stakeholders at several locations.
However, concerns were raised that participation had been inadequate, particularly among rural residents and tribal communities.
This prompted calls for another ground-level assessment in southern Rajasthan, with greater emphasis on hearing directly from the people most affected by decisions concerning the Aravalli region.

In its order dated September 7, the Supreme Court clarified that the committee must provide sufficient opportunities for all relevant stakeholders, including tribal communities in Rajasthan and Gujarat, to express their views.

During the upcoming inspections, the committee will examine several aspects of the region’s environmental and economic landscape, including mining and quarrying activities, including stone-crushing operations, forest cover, water sources and surrounding ecological conditions, existing land-use patterns and their environmental implications, the impact of mining and land-use practices on local residents and tribal livelihoods.
The committee will also seek feedback from environmentalists, subject experts, mining leaseholders, villagers, farmers, labourers and tribal communities.
Evening consultations are planned in both districts, with approximately three hours allocated for discussions with local residents and other stakeholders on each day.
According to the proposed schedule, the committee will complete its Gujarat tour by October 10 before entering southern Rajasthan on October 11.
On October 11, there will be field inspections in the Paldeval-Sarkan area of Dungarpur district, followed by consultations with stakeholders.
On October 12, inspection of the Kevadiya-Kothara area in Banswara district will be made followed by discussions with local communities and other stakeholders.
October 13 will mark the final day of the scheduled Rajasthan visit.

The inspections are expected to provide the committee with a clearer understanding of local environmental conditions, mining-related concerns and the socio-economic realities of communities living in the region.
The findings will form part of the broader assessment of the Aravalli hills’ definition, demarcation and conservation.
The committee’s report, due by November 30 this year, will be submitted to the Supreme Court for further consideration.
--IANS.

stories.summary: Justice Nagu was the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court immediately before his appointment on the Bench of the Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: Supreme Court judge, Justice Sheel Nagu, on Friday (October 9, 2026) recused himself from hearing an appeal filed by the State of Punjab against a State High Court order for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into corruption allegations linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann’s office.
Justice Nagu was the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court immediately before his appointment on the Bench of the Supreme Court.

When the case came up for hearing on October 8, Justice Dipankar Datta had orally indicated that Justice Nagu may have to recuse, but said the case file had not reached the latter judge, who would go through them and take a call.
On October 9, the court conveyed to the assembled courtroom that Justice Nagu had decided to withdraw, and the case would be reassigned to another Bench by the Chief Justice of India.

The State of Punjab, in its appeal before the apex court, has argued that the High Court's direction for a CBI probe suffered from errors such as treating information shared under Section 66(2) of the PMLA as a direction that makes registration “inevitable”, contrary to the 2022 decision of the apex court in the Vijay Madanlal Choudhary case.
The High Court had directed the CBI to probe corruption allegations linked to Chief Minister Mann’s office.

The allegations were raised by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) against public servants and private individuals linked to the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and include corruption in transfers and postings, policy manipulation, cash for tenders, and other serious irregularities.

Pronouncing its order on a public interest litigation case on October 5, the High Court Division Bench headed by Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra had said that, on a cumulative assessment of the material placed on record in the petition, the court was of the view that a fair and transparent investigation was required into the issue.

The petitioner in the High Court, advocate Nikhil Saraf, had argued that no action had been forthcoming despite communications from the ED under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 to the Punjab government.

stories.headline: Five former J&K cadre IAS officers among 33 transferred in Delhi
stories.title: Five former J&K cadre IAS officers among 33 transferred in Delhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 09: The Delhi Government has ordered the transfer and posting of 33 IAS officers belonging to the AGMUT and DANICS cadres, including five officers from the erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir cadre. Among the key appointments, senior IAS officer Navin Kumar Choudhary has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary (General Administration Department), while Bipul Pathak and Prashant Goyal have been assigned revised responsibilities in the Delhi administration. According to the government order, Bipul Pathak, a 1992-batch AGMUT cadre officer, will continue as Additional Chief Secretary (Social Welfare). He will also hold additional charges as Managing Director of the Delhi SC/ST/OBC Finance and Development Corporation and the Delhi Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Minorities and Handicapped Financial and Development Corporation. Pathak will additionally hold the posts of Additional Chief Secretary (SC/ST/OBC), Additional Chief Secretary (Women and Child Development) and Financial Commissioner. Prashant Goyal, a 1993-batch AGMUT cadre IAS officer, has been appointed Additional Chief Secretary (Power). He will also hold additional charges as Chairman and Managing Director of the Delhi Financial Corporation and the Delhi State Civil Supplies Corporation, besides serving as Additional Chief Secretary (Administrative Reforms) and Additional Chief Secretary (Health and Family Welfare). Navin Kumar Choudhary, a 1994-batch AGMUT cadre officer, has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary (General Administration Department). He was previously serving as Additional Chief Secretary (Irrigation and Flood Control), while also holding charge of the GAD. Choudhary will retain additional charge of the Irrigation and Flood Control Department and take on the additional responsibility of Additional Chief Secretary (Food and Civil Supplies). The order also assigns fresh responsibilities to officers who were awaiting postings. Prasanna Ramaswamy G, a 2010-batch AGMUT cadre officer, has been posted as Additional Commissioner in the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. Swati Sheemar, a 2023-batch AGMUT cadre IAS officer, has been appointed Additional Director (Education), replacing Patil Pranjal Lahensingh, who has been transferred to the Women and Child Development Department. The order covers 33 IAS officers from the AGMUT and DANICS cadres. Details of all transfers and postings were not available in the information provided.

stories.title: Supreme Court upholds Andhra Pradesh High Court judgment on BC reservations
stories.summary: A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu calls the High Court order ‘very reasonable’ and says there was no empirical data to justify breaching the 50% ceiling
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court dismissed the Andhra Pradesh government’s plea against the High Court (HC) judgment on reservations for the Backward Classes (BCs) in elections to rural and urban local bodies (ULBs).

The HC had earlier this week set aside G.O. Nos. 105 and 1065 through which the government sought to provide 34% reservation to BCs in Panchayat Raj Institutions (PRIs) and 33.33% quota in the ULBs, saying they exceeded the 50% threshold.

Hearing the special leave petition (SLP) filed by the State government on Friday (October 9, 2026), a Bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu turned down the State’s appeal, calling the HC order in the matter ‘very reasonable’.

Appearing for the State, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi submitted that there was no reason for the HC to reject as unreliable the data on the basis of which the percentages of reservation were determined by the State.
Justice Datta asked Mr. Rohatgi to tender an explanation as to how the HC erred in its judgment and on the relevance of the Unified Family Survey data.
The Supreme Court said the HC had rightly held that the reservations were beyond the 50% ceiling prescribed in the 1992 Indra Sawhney.
Union of India judgment, and there was no empirical data to justify the breach of that ceiling.

In a separate petition, a three-judge Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the elections could not be delayed on the ground that the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls was under way, and the existing rolls should be used if the situation warranted.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Against TN Speaker Dropping Disqualification Proceedings Over AIADMK MLAs' Cross-Voting
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses Plea Against TN Speaker Dropping Disqualification Proceedings Over AIADMK MLAs' Cross-Voting
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to interfere with the Madras High Court's dismissal of a public interest litigation (PIL) that sought to challenge the Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker's decision to drop disqualification proceedings against certain AIADMK MLAs who had voted against the party whip during a confidence motion in favour of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay of the TVK party.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana refused to entertain the petition filed by one PV Selvakumar in the "peculiar facts and circumstances of the case." The bench clarified that it has left the questions of law open.
During the hearing, the bench questioned the petitioner's locus standi.
The petitioner's counsel replied that the petitioner was not a member of the Assembly but was a member of AIADMK, who was aggrieved by the MLAs' conduct as a voter.
The Chief Justice noted that the petitioner did not belong to the political party in the relevant sense, while Justice Mohana observed that the party appeared to have condoned the action.
Justice Bagchi observed that to maintain proceeding under the tenth schedule, one needed to be a member.
"We are fully with you that sanctity of constitutional mandate must be preserved.
but we must understand workings of democratic sytem," Justice Bagchi said.
The counsel replied that democracy would be strengthened if a voter can pursue the disqualification action.
The bench however pointed out that the party appeared to have condoned the act of the defectors.

The court indicated it would have been more inclined to hear the matter if the party itself had taken a clear decision, and that any refusal by the Speaker to allow withdrawal of proceedings could have been agitated by the party.
The counsel insisted the issue was not limited to the whip and involved letters issued to the Speaker.

stories.title: Supreme Court refuses plea to ‘review’ order to quash FIRs against NEET-UG protestors
stories.summary: CJI says the orders was prompted by concern for students, their future
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) refused to review its September 1 direction to quash FIRs against students and youth who participated in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak protests and were subject to a brutal police crackdown on July 20 in the national capital.
The FIRs were quashed by the court using its extraordinary powers to administer complete justice under the Constitution.
“You have to appreciate… We do not use Article 142 in every situation.
We did it concerned for their parents.
These students have a long life.
They have future prospects, we don’t want them entangled in court proceedings,” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed advocate Mathews Nedumpara, who appeared for the petitioner.
Mumbai resident and senior citizen L. Ramanathan, in a petition filed through advocate Linto K.B., questioned the judicial overpowering of the basic police function to investigate a crime.

“The police, while discharging its statutory functions of investigation, must be permitted to investigate offences freely, fairly and without extraneous interference which include interim judicial directions passed at an interlocutory stage.
These interim directions have the effect of controlling, restraining, or micro-managing an ongoing investigation before its final outcome is tested on merits,” Mr. Nedumpara submitted.
Chief Justice Kant said there was a fine distinguishing line drawn in the September 1 order.
Only criminal cases registered against innocent protestors and students have been quashed.
The police were given liberty to continue with its investigation against hardened criminals.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Stays Trial In Criminal Defamation Cases Filed By BJP Leader Ramesh Bhiduri, Nephew Against TV Today Network
stories.title: Supreme Court Stays Trial In Criminal Defamation Cases Filed By BJP Leader Ramesh Bhiduri, Nephew Against TV Today Network
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today stayed the trial in criminal defamation cases filed against TV Today Network Ltd., which owns Aaj Tak and the India Today group, filed by BJP leader Ramesh Bidhuri and his nephew Rajpal Poswal.
The case concerns alleged defamatory news connecting Bhiduri's nephew to a gang rape and abduction case.
The case relates to a news broadcast aired in 2011 concerning a gang rape and abduction case involving an individual described as the brother-in-law of Bidhuri's nephew.
At the time, Bidhuri was an elected MLA from the Tughlakabad constituency.
The broadcast criticised alleged police inaction in arresting the individual, while his co-accused had already been taken into custody.
Complaints were filed by Bidhuri and Poswal alleging that the telecast was malicious, defamatory, misleading and intended to tarnish their reputation before the public.
On November 2025, the Delhi High Court dismissed petitions filed by TV Today challenging a trial court order which had rejected its applications for discharge.
The High Court held that the Metropolitan Magistrate did not have the power to discharge an accused in a summons triable case.
The High Court rejected the contention that the Magistrate could invoke inherent jurisdiction under Section 251 of the CrPC to drop proceedings.
The High Court further held that Section 251 of the CrPC does not empower a Magistrate to undertake a mini-trial or evaluate defences on merits at that stage.
The stage for consideration of such issues would arise only when evidence is led, the HC stated.

On November 2025, the Delhi High Court dismissed petitions filed by TV Today challenging a trial court order which had rejected its applications for discharge.
The High Court held that the Metropolitan Magistrate did not have the power to discharge an accused in a summons triable case.
The High Court rejected the contention that the Magistrate could invoke inherent jurisdiction under Section 251 of the CrPC to drop proceedings.
The High Court further held that Section 251 of the CrPC does not empower a Magistrate to undertake a mini-trial or evaluate defences on merits at that stage.

stories.headline: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court mulls having tribunals first hear deleted voters seeking re-inclusion
stories.title: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court mulls having tribunals first hear deleted voters seeking re-inclusion
stories.summary: The Court suggested lakhs of voters seeking inclusion in the West Bengal electoral roll should be heard first, while appeals for exclusion are taken up last
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) orally suggested that lakhs of voters seeking inclusion in the West Bengal electoral roll deserved to be heard first, while appeals for exclusion pending before the Appellate Tribunals could be heard last.

An affidavit filed by the Election Commission of India (EC) in the Supreme Court in September 2026 revealed that more than 22 lakh voters purged from the electoral roll during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in West Bengal, on grounds such as “logical discrepancies,” had filed appeals challenging their exclusion.
The EC affidavit had said that 16.10 lakh appeals had been filed against inclusion.
The poll body had said a total of 38.31 lakh appeals were filed in the tribunals in the State.
The 19 Appellate Tribunals are struggling under a massive backlog, with 37.05 lakh of the 38.31 lakh appeals currently stuck in limbo.
At the present pace, clearing the backlog will take more than 12 years, one of the petitioners, Congress leader Prasenjit Bose, has argued.

So far, the Appellate Tribunals, according to EC statistics, have disposed of only 3% of the total appeals filed, and 93% of these disposed-of appeals have resulted in the inclusion of electors in the electoral rolls.

In an oral mentioning, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Mr. Bose, and advocates Prashant Bhushan and Neha Rathi, representing five disentitled voters, said the disentitled voters in the State had already missed both the Assembly elections in May 2026 and the recent by-elections.
The lawyers said these voters should be allowed to cast their vote in the Municipal elections scheduled for November 2026, regardless of whether their appeals were pending before the tribunals.
“Over one lakh appeals were decided by the tribunals in the past six months, of which 93% have been ruled in favour of the deleted voters, ordering their re-inclusion in the voter list.
Taking this fact into consideration, voters whose appeals for re-inclusion are pending should be allowed to vote in the municipal elections,” Mr. Bhushan said.

He said the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation elections were coming up soon, and that voters in these areas whose appeals were pending before the tribunals should have their cases decided on a priority basis.

stories.headline: Kerala Home Minister takes indirect swipe at Centre over Pegasus surveillance
stories.title: Kerala Home Minister takes indirect swipe at Centre over Pegasus surveillance
stories.summary: At the Cocon 2026 conference in Kochi, Kerala Minister Ramesh Chennithala warned that spyware like Pegasus threatens national security, while Deputy NSA T V Ravichandran urged technological sovereignty amidst rising cyber incidents.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in summary weight 42
article_sentences: Kochi: Home and Vigilance Minister Ramesh Chennithala on Friday took an indirect swipe at the Centre over the Pegasus spyware controversy, alluding to allegations of surveillance in India while referring to the country as the “largest democratic country in the world” at the inauguration of the Cocon 2026 cybersecurity conference, organised by Kerala.
Police in Kochi.

Chennithala briefly touched upon the controversy surrounding Pegasus, the Israeli-developed spyware that has triggered concerns over allegations of surveillance targeting politicians, journalists, activists and other individuals.
Without elaborating on the issue or directly accusing any authority, he warned that intrusive digital intelligence tools threatened not only individual privacy but also national security.
“There are so many case studies in our day-to-day discussion about Pegasus.
This is an Israeli digital intelligence firm using spyware, Pegasus.
There are a lot of discussions about Pegasus and how it operates even in the biggest democratic country in the world, India.

There are so many questions we know that; I don't want to go into those details, but this kind of information is definitely threatening our normal life, not only the individual life, but the life of the country also,” Chennithala said in his inaugural address at the Grand Hyatt, Bolgatty in Kochi.
Stressing the need for safeguards, Chennithala said state use of intrusive surveillance tools must be subject to strict legal and institutional oversight.
“Ensure that state use of intrusive surveillance tools should be lawful, necessary, and proportionate, with independent oversight,” he said.

Referring to major cybersecurity incidents, including the SolarWinds breach and the Colonial Pipeline attack, the minister highlighted the vulnerabilities of digital infrastructure and the consequences of cyberattacks.
The two-day conference, organised by the Kerala.
